paragraphs.title: The Establishment of Jehoshaphat’s Kingdom and His Faithfulness

easy.explanation: Jehoshaphat reigned in the place of Asa his father.
He placed forces in all the fenced cities of Judah.
easy.q: What did Jehoshaphat place in all the fenced cities of Judah?

easy.explanation: He took away the high places and groves out of Judah.
easy.q: What did Jehoshaphat take away from Judah?

answers: Because he walked in the first ways of David and did not seek Baalim
Because he built cities of store
Because he received presents from Judah
medium.explanation: The passage connects the LORD’s presence with Jehoshaphat’s faithfulness and rejection of Baalim.
medium.q: Why was the LORD with Jehoshaphat?

answers: Judah brought him presents, and he had riches and honour
He lost the cities of Judah
medium.explanation: All Judah brought Jehoshaphat presents, and he had riches and honour in abundance.
medium.q: What happened because the LORD established the kingdom in Jehoshaphat’s hand?

medium.explanation: In this context, high places were elevated sites used for worship, which Jehoshaphat removed.
medium.q: In the KJV, what are “high places”?

answers: He reigned, strengthened Judah, followed the LORD, and removed pagan worship sites
He removed the cities, abandoned Judah, and built no defenses
He taught the law, received flocks, and appointed Philistine commanders
challenge.explanation: The passage presents this sequence of political strengthening and faithfulness to the LORD.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes Jehoshaphat’s actions in verses 1–6?

answers: He cared only about military matters
He combined national security with faithfulness to the LORD
challenge.explanation: The verses describe both the strengthening of the kingdom and obedience to the LORD.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Jehoshaphat’s strengthening the kingdom while removing the high places and groves?

challenge.explanation: Jehoshaphat walked in the first ways of his father David.
challenge.q: Whose example is specifically mentioned as the way Jehoshaphat followed?

paragraphs.title: Teaching the Torah in the Cities of Judah

easy.explanation: He sent them in the third year of his reign.
easy.q: In which year of his reign did Jehoshaphat send teachers through Judah?

easy.explanation: Jehoshaphat sent his princes, Levites, and priests.
easy.q: Who was sent to teach in the cities of Judah?

answers: The book of the law of the LORD
The book of the wars of Judah
easy.explanation: They taught with the book of the law of the LORD.
easy.q: What book did the teachers have with them?

medium.explanation: They went about throughout all the cities of Judah and taught the people.

answers: To teach the people the law of the LORD
To bring sheep to the king
medium.explanation: Their assignment was to teach the people from the book of the law.
medium.q: What was the purpose of sending the Levites and priests?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that they traveled from city to city throughout Judah.
medium.q: In verse 9, what does “went about throughout” mean?

answers: To carry the book from place to place without teaching
To bring instruction from the law to people in different cities
To replace the princes of the kingdom
challenge.explanation: The teachers traveled through Judah so that they could teach the people.
challenge.q: What does the order of the verses suggest was the purpose of the mission?

challenge.explanation: The passage names princes, Levites, and priests.
challenge.q: Which group of officials took part in the teaching mission?

challenge.explanation: These verses focus on teaching the people the law of the LORD.
challenge.q: What was the central activity in verses 7–9?

easy.explanation: The fear of the LORD fell upon the surrounding kingdoms.
easy.q: What caused the surrounding kingdoms not to make war against Jehoshaphat?

easy.explanation: Some of the Philistines brought him presents and tribute silver.
easy.q: Who brought Jehoshaphat presents and tribute silver?

easy.explanation: He built castles and cities of store in Judah.
easy.q: What did Jehoshaphat build in Judah?

answers: The fear of the LORD caused the kingdoms to attack Judah
The fear of the LORD kept the kingdoms from making war
The fear of the LORD caused Judah to abandon its cities
medium.explanation: The surrounding kingdoms made no war against Jehoshaphat because of the fear of the LORD.
medium.q: What relationship does the passage show between the fear of the LORD and Judah’s political situation?

answers: Flocks of thousands of rams and he goats
medium.explanation: The Arabians brought 7,700 rams and 7,700 he goats.
medium.q: What did the Arabians bring to Jehoshaphat?

medium.explanation: Castles were fortified places built for protection.

answers: Political security, gifts, construction, and prosperity
Teaching the law, removing groves, and appointing priests
challenge.explanation: The verses describe peace from surrounding kingdoms, gifts, building, and increasing greatness.
challenge.q: Which sequence of results appears in verses 10–13?

answers: Jehoshaphat held a strong political position
The cities of Judah had been deserted
challenge.explanation: The gifts and absence of war indicate Judah’s strength and influence.
challenge.q: What can the gifts from different peoples suggest about Jehoshaphat’s kingdom?

answers: The Arabians brought thousands of rams and he goats
He sent teachers through the cities
challenge.explanation: The large number of animals brought by the Arabians shows the abundance described.
challenge.q: Which detail especially demonstrates the abundance received by Jehoshaphat?

paragraphs.title: The Organization of the Army and Royal Service

easy.explanation: The passage lists military leaders and warriors from Judah and Benjamin.
easy.q: From which two tribes were the captains and mighty men listed?

easy.explanation: Adnah is named as the chief captain of Judah.
easy.q: Who was the first captain of Judah named?

answers: In the cities of the Philistines
easy.explanation: They served beside those whom the king placed in the fenced cities.
easy.q: Where were additional men stationed besides those listed?

answers: He willingly offered himself unto the LORD
medium.explanation: Amasiah is described as one who willingly offered himself unto the LORD.
medium.q: What is said about Amasiah the son of Zichri?

answers: Armed men with bow and shield
medium.explanation: Eliada had armed men with bow and shield.
medium.q: What kind of soldiers were with Eliada?

medium.explanation: The expression refers to military commanders over units of thousands.

answers: It was organized under commanders and units
It had no soldiers from Benjamin
challenge.explanation: The list identifies commanders, groups of warriors, and their numbers.
challenge.q: What does the list of names and numbers reveal about Jehoshaphat’s army?

answers: The first group served as teachers, and the last group were priests
The first group were listed captains and mighty warriors, while the last group were stationed in the fenced cities
The first group were Philistines, and the last group were Arabians
challenge.explanation: The passage lists military leaders and warriors, then adds those stationed in the fenced cities.
challenge.q: What distinction is made between the men listed in verses 14–18 and the men mentioned at the end?

answers: The mention of men with bow and shield and men ready for war
The mention of the book of the law
The mention of cities of store only
challenge.explanation: The passage identifies soldiers with different equipment and military roles.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the army included different kinds of soldiers?
